subject: Retention exception request & subprocessor/data-transfer checklist
messages:
From: Legal Ops (Acme Health) <legal-ops@acmehealth.com>
To: aisha_rahman@redwood.com
Cc: s.patel@procureco.com
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: log & backup retention extension for upcoming HIPAA audit

Hi Aisha,

We're reaching out to request a retention exception for Acme Health before their audit window opens next spring. Their compliance team needs backups and system logs retained for 18 months for a specific product integration (PatientSync). Our current DPA and default retention (90 days for hot snapshots, 365 days for archives) won't meet the audit scope.

Could you confirm whether Redwood can:
- Hold encrypted backup snapshots for 18 months (cold tier acceptable)
- Provide a list of all subprocessors that handle backups/logs and their locations
- Confirm whether cross-border transfers to EU subprocessor endpoints are required for these backups

Attached is the audit scope and the data categories in question. We also need a rough timeline for a DPA amendment and any procurement checklist items.

Appreciate a quick acknowledgement — Acme's legal team is hoping to have an answer this week.

Thanks,
Lisa Moreno
Legal Operations, Acme Health
[Attachment: acme-audit-scope.pdf]

From: aisha_rahman@redwood.com

1) I'll kick this over to Legal & Compliance (cc'd: Kimberly) to scope a DPA amendment / retention carveout.

3) Samir (ProcureCo), can you confirm the exact account IDs/environments that need the 18-month retention so we can create a scoped exception?

I've attached our standard retention-exception-form and a current subprocessor checklist to make responses easier. If everyone's aligned we can aim for a mutual action plan by EOD Friday.

Regards,

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: aisha_rahman@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 17 Dec 2026 11:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: log & backup retention extension for upcoming HIPAA audit

Aisha / Kimberly —

Operational notes:
- 18-month retention is feasible if we move eligible snapshots to cold tier after 30 days. That reduces cost and keeps retrieval within the SLA (24-48 hours for cold restore).
- We will encrypt at rest using Redwood-managed keys by default; customer KMS (Bring Your Own Key) is possible but requires Private deployment or an additional KMS integration ticket (time + procurement).
- Subprocessors: current backup storage is handled by CloudVendor (us-west, eu-west) and a long-term archive partner (third-party cold store in us-central). I'll need to confirm whether any archived replicas exist in EU for Acme's account; preliminary check shows replication to eu-west only for high-availability zones.

Action items for this thread:
- Aisha: get the exact environment IDs and product names (PatientSync production? staging?) from Acme.
- Kimberly / Legal: advise on amendment language and whether a carveout to DPA (temporary vs permanent) is acceptable.
- Marissa (billing): we should propose cost estimate — incremental storage + retrieval fees.

Related: I added a note to HubSpot (link below) and flagged this as a potential DPA amendment. If Legal wants, we can offer an SLA exception with a limited-duration MOA.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Infrastructure Product
[Related link: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/ACME-9876]

Thanks Aisha / Karthik —

Acme confirms PatientSync production (env: prod-ps-01) and a secondary analytics stream (env: analytics-ps-02) need the 18-month window. I've attached a data map that shows the flow and labels the artifacts they'd like preserved.

Two clarifying Qs from procurement/legal:
- Can Redwood produce a signed MOA/DPA amendment in advance of implementation? If so, what is the typical lead time?
- Does Redwood provide SOC2 artifact excerpts (control narrative + test results) for subprocessor handling of backups, or do we route that request to CloudVendor?

We'd like a proposed mutual action plan by Monday.

Best,
Samir Patel

From: aisha_rahman@redwood.com
To: legal-ops@acmehealth.com, s.patel@procureco.com
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: log & backup retention extension for upcoming HIPAA audit — Proposed plan

Lisa / Samir — thanks for the quick turn. Below is a proposed mutual action plan and timeline; please advise on any redlines.

Scope:
- Environments: prod-ps-01, analytics-ps-02
- Data classes: system logs, application-level backups, snapshot images referenced in Acme data map
- Retention window: 18 months (540 days) from creation date; snapshots moved to cold tier after 30 days

Operational commitments:
- Redwood will enable cold-tier retention for the two environments and maintain encrypted copies for 540 days.
- Retrieval SLA for cold restores: 48 hours standard; expedited option 8 hours (additional fee).
- Encryption: Redwood-managed keys by default; BYOK available under Private deployment (separate order).

Legal / Compliance commitments:
- Redwood Legal (cc: Kimberly) will draft a DPA amendment (retention carveout + MOA) and circulate for signature within 5 business days of account confirmation and subprocessor sign-off.
- Subprocessor disclosure: we will provide a current subprocessor registry and SOC2 summaries from CloudVendor where available; full third-party attestations may require vendor coordination (estimated 3–7 business days).

Commercials / Billing:
- Marissa will produce an estimate for incremental cold storage + monthly monitoring and a one-time setup fee for the retention carveout.

Attachments & next steps:
- Attached: retention-exception-form.pdf (filled by Acme would speed approval), Acme data map received, subprocessor-checklist.csv
- Action: Samir to confirm acceptance of scope and return the filled retention-exception-form by Thursday, Dec 23.
- Action: Kimberly to propose DPA amendment language by Wednesday, Dec 22.

If that timeline works I'll move the request to Legal & Compliance intake and mark it high priority. Appreciate the collaboration — we'll aim to keep the rollout non-disruptive.

Regards,
Aisha Rahman
Senior Sales Ops, Redwood Inference
